ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a massless spring with an original length of $10\mathrm{cm}$ is fixed at one end to an object with mass $m=4\mathrm{kg}$, and a horizontal force $F$ is applied at the other end. (Assume that the maximum static friction is equal to the kinetic friction, and the spring always remains within its elastic limit, $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$).

1. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the horizontal surface is 0.45, and when the spring is stretched to $14.5\mathrm{cm}$, the object just moves to the right at a constant velocity, what is the spring constant?
2. If the spring is compressed to $6\mathrm{cm}$, what is the frictional force acting on the object?
3. If the spring is compressed to $16\mathrm{cm}$, what is the frictional force acting on the object?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$400\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$
$16\mathrm{N}$, direction horizontally to the right
$18\mathrm{N}$, direction horizontally to the left

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figures show a rectangular block resting on a horizontal rough surface. A horizontal spring is connected to the block on its right side, and the free right end of the spring is acted on by a horizontal force F directed to the right. I take rightward as the positive direction. Reasoning: The normal force on the block is N = mg = 4 × 10 = 40 N. Since the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.45 and the maximum static friction is stated to equal the kinetic friction, the friction limit is f_max = μmg = 0.45 × 4 × 10 = 18 N. 1. When the spring length is 14.5 cm, its natural length is 10 cm, so the extension is 4.5 cm = 0.045 m. The object moves right at constant velocity, so the net force on it is zero. The spring pulls the block to the right and kinetic friction acts to the left with magnitude 18 N. Thus k × 0.045 = 18, so k = 18 / 0.045 = 400 N/m. 2. When the spring length is 6 cm, it is compressed by 10 cm − 6 cm = 4 cm = 0.04 m. The compressed spring pushes the block to the left with force kx = 400 × 0.04 = 16 N. Since 16 N is less than the maximum static friction 18 N, the block can remain at rest, and static friction balances this force. Therefore the friction on the block is 16 N to the right. 3. For the stated 16 cm case, following the assigned interpretation, treat this as an actual spring length of 16 cm, i.e. the spring is stretched by 16 cm − 10 cm = 6 cm = 0.06 m. The spring pulls the block to the right with force kx = 400 × 0.06 = 24 N, which exceeds the friction limit 18 N. Therefore the block would move right, and the friction is kinetic/limiting friction of magnitude 18 N to the left.
